rule: Sources are evidence for generalized craft principles only. Never use source names, artists, studios, titles, exact faces, exact costumes, exact palettes, signature rendering, or named-style phrases as production prompt targets.

sources.source: Buddy Daddies official interview with Katsumi Enami
sources.observedProblem: Initial visual assumptions can be wrong before personality is understood.
generalizedPrinciples: understand personality before locking body type, face, hair and clothing
a character concept may require structural redesign when deeper personality information contradicts the first visual stereotype
body build is part of character interpretation, not a neutral mannequin
yoruTranslation: Living Visual and story facts precede costume polish
do not preserve a visually attractive body or face choice if it contradicts established personhood
when a design feels generic, first check whether the body/face was chosen before the person was understood

sources.source: Buddy Daddies official interview with animation character designer Soichiro Sako
sources.observedProblem: A stylish source design can become rigid if it cannot deform for comedy or move for action.
generalizedPrinciples: character design should preserve appeal while supporting comedic deformation
facial design should allow a broad acting range rather than staying beautiful and rigid
action scenes should be anticipated in the clothing and body design
ensemble contrast can be built from physique and posture, not only color or costume
yoruTranslation: Character Masters must support serious scenes, trivial conversation, comedy and action
evaluate pair/group contrast through body and posture
do not make high-resolution beauty incompatible with four-panel acting

sources.source: Bandai Namco Tales 30th Anniversary interview with Kosuke Fujishima
sources.observedProblem: World cohesion, historical plausibility and travel practicality can conflict with individual character uniqueness.
generalizedPrinciples: clothing should avoid obvious practical inconvenience for the character's journey and daily activity
technology and garment details should make sense for the imagined period/world
overly strict unified aesthetics can erase party-member individuality
regional and cultural differences can emerge from imagining how characters actually live
silhouette can be deliberately used to create a new role within an ensemble
yoruTranslation: era and location affect fasteners, materials, storage and wear habits
world grammar is a shared toolkit, not a uniform
every party member must keep an individual silhouette and life-specific clothing logic

sources.source: Bandai Namco Studios Making of Tales of Arise Part 1
sources.observedProblem: Character design, material depiction and rendering can become disconnected if visual style is treated as a post-process.
generalizedPrinciples: character design can incorporate material and world-visual decisions developed by the art-direction team
metal, cloth and other material treatments should participate in worldbuilding
rendering style should be researched as part of the title's visual identity rather than copied from an external reference
technical rendering and character design should reinforce each other
yoruTranslation: paper, ink, lantern light and old-star-chart qualities must affect construction/material/light behavior, not only motifs
rendering authority remains separate from character identity authority
Yoru rendering should be derived from its own world material system

sources.source: Cygames Magazine interview with Umamusume art director
sources.observedProblem: Large casts and multiple visual formats can become generic when production efficiency reuses the same poses, expressions and presentation.
generalizedPrinciples: believability grows from careful depiction of friendship, effort and everyday life, not only spectacle
individual poses, expressions and acting choices help make large casts feel like distinct people
2D, 3D and chibi each have different strengths and should not be forced into identical presentation logic
art direction supervises overall balance across specialized teams and formats
small scene-specific details accumulate into character familiarity
yoruTranslation: ordinary conversation is a design-validation environment
Character Master, chibi and pixel are different reductions of one identity rather than separate character designs
do not reuse one acting template across the whole cast
review the whole game's visual balance, not only isolated hero art

crossSourceConsensus: personality and life should influence body, face, clothing and posture
practical movement and daily use matter
ensemble identity must survive shared world aesthetics
acting range is part of character design quality
material/rendering decisions should arise from the project's own world
art direction is an iterative supervision process rather than a one-shot generation prompt
promotionRule: A researched principle may enter the Philosophy or Craft Master only after it is generalized, translated to Yoru no Shirube, stripped of source-specific expression, and checked against current canon and user-confirmed preferences.
